text:
devon: ran a 10k-request perf sweep for draft handoff between qwen-7b-draft and mixtral-8x-quant, seeing 95th tail jump ~2.4x around step 1200, looks correlated with KV churn and a kernel fallback.
elaine: can you paste the profiler snippet?
devon: sure, short excerpt:
```
[kernel_select] model=qwen-7b-draft selected=matmul_fast_v3 latency=0.9ms
[kernel_select] model=mixtral-8x-quant fallback=matmul_generic latency=2.7ms
[kv_cache] evict_rate spike at step=1203, hit_rate down 18% -> 62%
[spec_decode] acceptance_rate for drafts=0.21 (target ~0.4)
```
samir: interesting — fallback to matmul_generic explains the latency step. why is mixtral hitting the generic kernel while qwen stays on fast one?
rik: my guess: quant kernel matcher uses head_dim & kv_layout signature; mixtral-quant kernel got mismatched due to ROPE scaling patch (we bumped rope base for longer sequences).
maria: +1. earlier change to RoPE scaling multiplier for mixtral may have changed stride computation. that would change kernel hash and force fallback.
devon: that fits with KV churn: if layout changed, KV cache can't reuse entries and we evict more often.
elaine: what about tokenizer mismatch between qwen draft outputs and mixtral accept check? acceptance_rate 0.21 is low, could cause lots of speculative retries and extra decoding steps -> extra KV writes.
samir: true — speculative decoding is magnifying the kernel mismatch effects. more speculative forks => more open KV windows, more memory pressure.
rik: proposed fixes: 1) add kernel signature compatibility layer for quantized mixtral (cheap shim) 2) revert rope-scale tweak on canary and retest 3) tune draft acceptance_threshold up to 0.35 and run 50k sample to measure latency/cost tradeoff.
maria: also try prefix-aware KV keying: when family changes but tokenstream prefix matches, reuse cache entries. maybe conservative but helpful.
devon: created perf issue: https://redwood/issue/INF-2387 assigned to @rik, added logs and the 10k trace. will run the acceptance threshold canary later today.
infra-bot: canary deploy scheduled to eng-runtime-canary at 2026-11-03T21:30Z by rik.
elainE: (typo) meant: thanks everyone. small note — when you run the 50k sample, include sequence-length buckets (<=64, 65-256, 257-1024) and capture kernel_select histograms per bucket.
samir: ack, will add bucketed traces.
rik: quick command I'm running locally:
```bash
python infra/perf/run_sweep.py --models qwen-7b-draft,mixtral-8x-quant --speculative --acceptance 0.35 --buckets 64,256,1024 --out /tmp/sweep-1942.json
```
devon: if canary looks good we should also push a routing policy fallback that prefers same-family pairing for speculative decoding to avoid cross-family churn. lower perf but more stable.
maria: +1 for routing policy toggle behind feature flag. we can A/B it.
devon: ok, next steps: rik implements the kernel shim, samir runs bucketed 50k sweep with new acceptance, I'll prototype routing toggle. we'll reconvene after results. :thumbsup:
